=== idx 485 ===
**Yes — header full width is the better model** for this surface.

### Recommended layout

```
[ App sidebar ]  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
                 │  Connectors › Discord › discord  · active │  ← full width of main pane
                 │  Overview  Feeds  Actions  Settings       │
                 ├──────────────┬────────────────────────────┤
                 │ CONNECTIONS  │  tab body                   │
                 │  + Add       │  (settings form, feeds…)    │
                 │  discord     │                            │
                 └──────────────┴────────────────────────────┘
```

### Why this wins

| | Header full width + rail under | Rail beside header (current) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Where am I** | Title spans the page; breadcrumb is one clear strip | Title competes with CONNECTIONS for the top-left |
| **Consistency** | Same as most admin UIs (GitHub, Linear, Stripe): chrome on top, context nav under | Odd hybrid |
| **Chat vs data** | Same shell; only tab body changes | Same, but header feels squeezed |
| **Empty rail** | “No connections found” sits under tabs, doesn’t steal title row | Rail at top next to “Local Install” feels like a second app nav |

### What stays the same

- Same tab bar on connector + connection  
- Same connections tree (expand feeds under the open connection)  
- Settings / Overview / Feeds / Actions still scope by tab  

### Tab behavior (separate, but pairs well)

- **Don’t hard-disable** Overview on chat — keep it clickable with the “live chat / no sync” empty state  
- Feeds / Actions: enabled with empty states until Discord publishes channels/ops; only disable if you truly have nothing to show *and* no CTA  

### Rule of thumb

- **Page identity** (breadcrumb, name, status) → full width top  
- **In-page navigation** (connections list) → under that, left of the body  

So: **header full width is the best model** for what you’re building.

### What **Discord · BYO** is

The connection header caption is built like this:

```349:353:packages/owletto/src/app/$owner/connectors/$connectorKey.$connectionId.tsx

  headerCaption ??
  errorText ??
  [connectorDef?.name ?? connection.connector_key, credentialMode]

```

with:

```132:135:packages/owletto/src/app/$owner/connectors/$connectorKey.$connectionId.tsx
const CREDENTIAL_MODE_LABEL = {
  managed: "Managed",
  byo: "BYO",
} as const;
```

So **Discord · BYO** means:

| Part | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Discord** | Connector display name |
| **BYO** | **Bring Your Own** credentials — you pasted bot token / app id / public key |

`effective_credential_mode` is only two values (plus null):

| Mode | Meaning | Typical path |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **`managed`** | Lobu-hosted install (“Add to Slack”, GitHub App, etc.) | OAuth install Lobu owns |
| **`byo`** | You supplied the secret | API key, bot token, custom OAuth app, etc. |
| **`null`** | Unresolved | Caption is just `"Discord"` |

Discord uses `auth: none` + options schema (bot credentials) → almost always **BYO**.

### Yes — there’s duplication

On that page you already have:

| Surface | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| **Breadcrumb** | `Connectors › Discord › discord` |
| **Title** | connection display name (`discord`) |
| **Status badge** | `active` |
| **Caption** | `Discord · BYO` |
| **Rail** | `discord` again |

So **“Discord” appears twice** (breadcrumb + caption), and **“discord” twice** (title + rail). Caption’s only *new* info is **BYO**.

Comments say facets moved out of the header into Settings, and chat is supposed to show Managed/BYO in the header instead of an auth-profile block — but stuffing it into a second line next to the product name is noisy.

**Cleaner model:** drop connector name from the caption; put credential mode on the **title row as a small badge** (like `active`):

### Drop the chips / caption clutter

Agree. On a connection page you already have:

- Breadcrumb: `Connectors › Discord › discord`
- Title: connection name  
- Status: `active`  
- Rail: same connection  

So **no** `Discord · BYO`, **no** facet chips in the header, **no** Managed/BYO badge unless you’re fixing a real ambiguity (e.g. two installs of the same Slack workspace). Settings (or create flow) is where auth *method* lives.

┌ App nav ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

| **Header (full width)** | Icon + breadcrumb + **title** (current page) + **status** only |
| **Tabs (full width)** | Shared: Overview · Feeds · Actions · Settings |
| **Under tabs** | **Left:** connections rail · **Right:** tab body |

I read the grok session (25 turns, `sidebar-entity-icons-agents-flat`) and the code it produced. Nothing is committed — 18 modified files sitting uncommitted in the owletto submodule of that worktree. So throwing the IA out is cheap.

## Why those 25 rounds didn't converge

Look at what the rounds were actually about: sidebar left vs right, header full-width vs rail, tab margins, disabled vs empty tabs, `Discord · BYO` caption, rail→tabs→rail. Every one of those was a *rendering* fix. None of them touched the reason the page feels wrong.

The page is a 1:1 projection of the schema. Tables became tabs:

| Table | UI |
|---|---|
| `connector_definition` | Connector page |
| `connection` | Connections tab → Connection page |
| `feed` | Feeds tab → Feed page |
| `operation` | Actions tab |
| `run` | Overview tab |
| `auth_profile` / `app_profile` | Settings + create form |

Concrete tells in the code:

- **`connector-tabs.ts:11-23`** — two tab sets with identical shape, and the middle slot swaps `Connections`↔`Feeds` *so the bar doesn't resize*. A layout constraint is being used as information architecture. Same word ("Overview", "Actions", "Settings") means a different thing at each depth.
- **Your screenshot** — Discord connector, zero connections, and Overview renders a runs table with `All / Sync / Action / Auth` + "All statuses" + "No runs yet". That's the `run.kind` enum shipped straight to the user.
- **`$connectorKey.$connectionId.tsx:197-200`** — `facets.chat` and `has_operations` decide tab labels and empty states. Internal resolution flags driving nav.
- **`facets.ts:39-51`** — 11 filter chips mixing three unrelated axes: what it does (data/chat/actions/inference/runtime), how it authenticates (oauth/api_key/app_install/device), and state (needs_setup).
- **`connection-form.tsx` — 2777 lines.** One form exposing auth profiles, app profiles, account profiles, browser auth profiles, device pick, CDP URL, MCP URL, and raw `options_schema`. This is the answer to your "I see other fields in there and not sure what makes sense."

Net: 2 levels × 4 tabs = 8 cells, and for Discord 4 of them are empty states. You've been polishing the frame around mostly-empty rooms.

## The rule I'd design against

**A screen per user decision, not a tab per table.**

There are four decisions a user makes here — connect something, choose what it can see, fix it when it breaks, disconnect — and two things they read: is it healthy, and what does it give my agents. Nothing in that list is "definition version", "run kind", "credential mode", or "auth profile slug". Those are evidence, and evidence only earns screen space when it explains a state the user has to act on.

## Three shapes

**A — Connection-first.** The list *is* connections (accounts), not connector types. "Discord" as a page mostly disappears; picking a connector is a step in Add, not a destination. Kills the intermediate hop that made `/connectors/create` feel duplicated. Cost: install/uninstall/version/workspace-auth need a home (an admin "Manage app" panel).

**B — Capability-first.** Reframe around the agent: Sources (what it reads), Tools (what it can call), Chat (where it talks). Connections become an implementation detail inside each. Best story for "what can my agent do", worst for "my Gmail is broken" — one broken account now shows up in three places.

**C — One page, no tabs.** Keep connector→connection, but the connection page is a single column of sections that render only when non-empty. Smallest change, and it deletes every empty tab.

## What I'd build

A+C. Connection is the noun; no tabs anywhere; feeds stop being a route depth.

```
Connectors                                       [+ Add]
  ● Slack · Acme workspace     2 channels          healthy
  ● Gmail · Work               Inbox syncing       2m ago
  ⚠ GitHub · Old fork          reauth needed       [Fix]
```

```
[icon] Work Gmail                                ● healthy
       Google Workspace · connected 3 Jul

What it brings in                                [+ Add]
  Inbox      collected    2m ago    1,204 items
  Sent       virtual      —

What agents can do            ← section omitted entirely at zero
  gmail.send_email, gmail.search                 [Try]

Settings ▾   name · auth · scope · remove        ← collapsed
```

Runs are not a tab — "Last synced 2m ago" plus a link into the Activity section you already have, filtered to this connection. Feeds open inline/drawer instead of route depth 5. `/connectors/discord` with exactly one connection redirects to that connection. The 11 facet chips collapse to one axis (Data · Chat · Tools); auth method is not something users browse by.

Two calls are genuinely yours before I'd design further:

A few things I can expand on if useful:

- **What I'm assuming about your users** — that most orgs run one connection per connector, so the connector page is usually a one-row list. If multi-connection is actually the common case (multiple Slack workspaces, several Gmail accounts), the connector level earns its place and my recommendation flips.

- **Whether the whole section is even the right container** — sandboxes and inference providers are folded into this same list as synthesized rows (`buildSandboxConnectorRows`, `buildInferenceConnectorRows`). They're not connections and don't have feeds. That may be a separate problem worth splitting off, or it may be the thing forcing the generic shape in the first place.
- **Scope of the redo** — whether you want to reshape the existing pages, or go further and reconsider the Add flow (that 2777-line form) at the same time. They're coupled: the form's shape is downstream of the same "expose the schema" instinct.

content.text:
Approach this as the design lead at a small studio known for their versatility, giving every client a visual identity pitched at the treatment the task actually calls for. Make deliberate choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this subject, and avoid templated designs.

## Read the request first

Calibrate treatment, not whether to design. A doc deserves the same craft as a landing page — what changes is the treatment that craft is delivered in.

Many requests call for a more utilitarian treatment: a plan, a memo, a demo. Make it polished: include real typographic hierarchy, considered spacing, and a proper palette, but avoid over-designing. Most pages do not need a flashy, gigantic hero. Keep flourishes tasteful and limited.

Some requests call for an editorial treatment: a landing page, a game, an app or tool they'll keep or share.

When unsure: a well-composed page is never the wrong answer; an over-designed visual identity sometimes is.

Fundamentals below apply to everything. The editorial process after that runs only when the read above says so.

## Fundamentals for every artifact

**Honor what's already there** Look for an existing design system first — CLAUDE.md, a tokens or theme file, existing component styles. When one exists, apply it; everything below fills gaps and never overrides. Precedence is always: the user's own words, then the project's existing system, then your choices.

**Ground it in the subject.** If the subject isn't already clear, pin it: one concrete subject, its audience, and the page's single job. The subject's own world — its materials, instruments, vernacular — is where distinctive choices come from. Build with real content throughout, never lorem.

**Pair typefaces** Typography carries the page even when the page isn't about typography. The Artifact CSP blocks font CDNs, so don't link a webfont URL and risk a silent fallback. Instead inline the face as a @font-face data URI. Keep running text near 65 characters wide; set a type scale and stay on it; give headings `text-wrap: balance`, body text room to breathe, and uppercase labels a touch of letter-spacing.

**Choose neutrals, don't default to them.** A pure mid-grey reads as unconsidered; a grey with a slight hue bias toward the page's accent reads as chosen. Pure white and near-black are fine grounds when they suit the subject — the point is that the neutral was picked, not inherited.

**Design both themes.** The page renders in the viewer's theme: `prefers-color-scheme` carries the OS preference, and the viewer's toggle stamps `data-theme="dark"` / `data-theme="light"` on the root element, which must override the media query in both directions. The robust pattern is token-level: define the palette as custom properties on `:root`, redefine only the tokens under `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` — style components through the tokens, never directly inside the media query — then redefine them again under `:root[data-theme="dark"]` and `:root[data-theme="light"]`. Give the second theme the same care as the first — don't naively invert; keep contrast legible and the accent working on both grounds. A design that deliberately commits to one visual world (a neon arcade screen, a letterpress invitation) may stay single-theme — make it a choice, not an omission.

**Let layout do the spacing.** Lay out sibling groups with flex or grid and `gap`, not per-element margins that silently collapse or double. Wide content — tables, code, diagrams — gets `overflow-x: auto` on its own container so the page body never scrolls sideways. Reach for `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` wherever digits line up in columns.

**Avoid AI-generated design** AI-generated design currently clusters around a few looks: warm cream (#F4F1EA) with a serif display and terracotta accent; near-black with a lone acid-green or vermilion pop; broadsheet hairline rules with dense columns; a purple-to-blue gradient hero on white; Inter or Space Grotesk as the "safe" face; emoji as section markers; everything centered; `rounded-lg` everywhere; accent bar/rail on rounded cards. Where the user pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly — their words always win, including when they ask for one of these looks. Where nothing is specified, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults.

**Build cleanly** Be cognizant of overlapping elements, cascade collisions, silent font fallbacks; visual bugs hide in the gap between source and output. Close every non-void element, double-quote attributes, give keyboard focus a visible state, respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. For generative or decorative graphics, reach for Canvas or WebGL rather than hand-authoring long SVG path data.

**CSS rules** When writing the CSS, watch your selector specificities. It is easy to generate classes that cancel each other out — a type-based selector like `.section` fighting an element-based one like `.cta` over padding and margins between sections. Structure the cascade so it doesn't silently undo your spacing.

**Writing the copy** Words are design material, not decoration. Write from the user's side of the screen — name things by what people recognize, not how the system is built (a person manages *notifications*, not *webhook config*). Active voice; a control says exactly what happens ("Publish", then a toast that says "Published"). Errors explain what went wrong and how to fix it — no apologies, no vagueness. Specific beats clever.

**Structure is information** Structural devices, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, should encode something true about the content, not decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence - like a real process or a typed timeline where order carries information the reader needs. Question if choices like numbered markers actually make sense before incorporating them.

**When it's a UI, not a document** A dashboard or tool is scanned and operated, not read top-to-bottom, so the craft shifts from typography to information design. Surface the summary before the detail; encode state in form as well as number — a pill, a chip, a severity stripe — so what needs attention reads at a glance. Semantic color (good / warning / critical) is separate from the accent hue and doesn't count as your accent. Give sparklines and charts the same care as type: an area fill, a faint grid, an emphasized endpoint. What's interactive should look interactive.



## Process

Before writing code, sketch a short design plan — a compact token system with color, type, and layout:
- **Color**: describe the palette as 4–6 named hex values.
- **Type**: typefaces for 2+ roles — a characterful display face used with restraint, a complementary body face, and a utility face for captions or data if needed.
- **Layout**: a layout concept in one or two sentences.

Then build, following the plan and deriving every color and type decision from it.

## When the request is editorial

The stance shifts: the client has already rejected proposals that felt templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view. Make opinionated calls, and take one real aesthetic risk where it serves the work.

Review the design plan against the subject before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page, revise that part, and note what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the plan's uniqueness do you write the code, following the revised plan exactly.

**Principles** 

- The hero is a thesis: open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world — headline, image, live demo, interactive moment. 
- Typography carries the personality of the page. Pair the display and body faces deliberately, not the same families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. Make the type treatment itself a memorable part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content. 
- Leverage motion deliberately. Think about where and if animation can serve the subject: a page-load sequence, a scroll-triggered reveal, hover micro-interactions, ambient atmosphere. An orchestrated moment usually lands harder than scattered effects; choose what the direction calls for. However, sometimes less is more, and extra animation contributes to the feeling that the design is AI-generated. 
- Match complexity to the vision. Maximalist directions need elaborate execution; minimal directions need precision in spacing, type, and detail. Elegance is executing the chosen vision well.
- Spend your boldness in one place; keep everything around it quiet. If the accent fights the ground, shift it toward analogous or drop saturation rather than replacing it.

content.text:
I have the ground truth I need. Now the design plan, then the build.

**Palette** — cool slate-bias ground (`#101219` dark / `#F6F5F2` light) so it reads as tooling, not editorial; `--signal` warm ochre `#D9A24E`/`#A96A16` reserved *only* for what's proposed-new; semantic green/amber/clay live strictly inside the mock screens as UI state, never as doc chrome. Old/rejected is grey + strike, never a second accent.

**Type** — three roles: Charter/Iowan serif for spec voice (separates the document from the thing it specifies), system sans inside every mock so the screens read as the real app, and SF Mono for plate numbers, connector keys (`google.gmail`), and field names — the vernacular of the subject.

**Layout** — a plate sequence. Each plate: mono eyebrow (`04/17 · CONNECTION · CHAT`), one-line thesis, a full-fidelity HTML mock in a chrome frame, then a two-column notes grid — what's shown, and what the old design showed here that's now gone. Numbering earns its place because the plates trace the actual product flow.

Proposal · unbuilt · supersedes the tabbed shell

One screen per decision, not one tab per table.

The current connector pages are a projection of the schema. Six tables became six tabs, and for a chat connector four of the eight resulting cells render an empty state. Every round of feedback so far has moved margins around that structure without touching it.

What follows is seventeen plates covering every page, every connector type, and every subpage under a different premise: the interface shows what a person can decide or fix, and nothing else. Field names, run kinds, credential modes, and profile slugs appear only where they change what someone has to do.

What the pages are doing today

Diagnosis

Tabs are named after storage, so the same four words mean different things at each depth, and the middle slot swaps Connections↔Feeds purely so the bar does not resize. A layout constraint became the information architecture.

TableBecameShould be
connector_definitionConnector page + 4 tabsA catalog entry, and an admin panel
connectionConnections tab → page + 4 tabsThe page. The only page.
feedFeeds tab → its own route depthA section, opening in place
operationActions tab (empty for chat)A section, absent at zero
runOverview tab with kind filtersOne line, linking to Activity
auth_profileSettings + a 2,777-line formSetup, then invisible until broken

The premise every plate is built on

A screen per user decision, not a tab per table.

There are four decisions here — connect something, choose what it can see, fix it when it breaks, disconnect — and two things people read: is it healthy, and what does it give my agents. Everything else is evidence, and evidence earns space only when it explains a state someone has to act on.

Structural moves

  • Connection is the noun. The list is accounts, not connector types.
  • No tab bar anywhere. Sections render only when non-empty.
  • Feeds stop being a route depth — they open in place.
  • /connectors/discord with one connection redirects to it.
  • The connector level survives only as Manage app, an admin panel.
  • Eleven filter chips collapse to three, on one axis.

Depths removed

  • Two ways to add a connection collapse into one.

Seventeen plates, each a full-fidelity mock plus two note columns — what the screen serves, and what the current design showed there that's now gone.

The coverage:

**Flow** — index (01), catalog (02), and three setup screens split by auth shape: managed install (03, Slack), OAuth-then-scope (04, Gmail), BYO credentials (05, Discord). That last split is the answer to your create-page question — one form can't serve `app_installation`, `oauth`, and `auth: none` without becoming the 2,777-line thing it is.

**Connector types** — chat (06, Slack: no sync section, no tools section, because `kind: "integration"` genuinely has neither), data+one tool (07, Gmail), data+nine tools (08, GitHub — the density stress test for no-tabs), broken (09), device-pinned (10), inbound webhook (11), your-own-database (12).

**Subpages** — a collected source opening inline instead of at route depth five (13), and a channel rendered as a transcript because a streaming feed has no sync history to show (14).

**Not connections** — inference provider (15) and sandbox (16) get their own page shapes instead of synthesized rows with disabled tabs. Then Manage app (17), which is where install/uninstall/version/workspace-auth land once the connector level stops being a destination.

Two things worth your attention beyond the screens. The **ledger** at the bottom is the literal answer to "without exposing the API as it is" — twelve fields, where each was rendered, and where it went. And the three open questions at the end are the ones I couldn't decide for you: whether one-connection-per-connector is really typical (the whole collapse rests on it), whether the numbers carrying these pages actually exist yet (`event_count` is deliberately omitted from list responses for cost — if per-source counts need building, that's PR one, not a detail), and whether Settings stays a disclosure or becomes a route.

**Confidence: high on the diagnosis, medium on the design.** The diagnosis is grounded — I read `connector-tabs.ts`, both route files, the real connector definitions in `packages/connectors/src`, and the `ConnectionItem`/`FeedItem` shapes, so every field named in the ledger is a real field and every connector behaviour shown is real. The design is one considered proposal, unvalidated against users, and plate 01's sort-broken-first and plate 09's "62 items behind" assume data I haven't confirmed is queryable.

Next actions you could pick from:

- Answer question 02 first — I can grep the server for whether per-feed item counts and per-tool usage counts are already queryable, since that gates roughly half these screens.
- Pick 2–3 plates to build for real against the running dev server, rather than committing to all seventeen.
- Let me diff this against the uncommitted work in `sidebar-entity-icons-agents-flat` and tell you what survives — some of it (removing the Feeds tab, un-disabling tabs) points the same direction.
- Or push back on a specific plate and I'll rework it; the file redeploys to the same URL.

That question lands exactly on the constraint. Checking `useConnectionConnectorGroups` — the index **already** returns connections, just nested: each group carries `connections: ConnectionGroupSummary[]`. And `useConnections(orgId)` with no filter returns full `ConnectionItem[]` (status, `error_message`, `feed_count`, `operations_summary`, device fields). So a connection-first list needs **zero API change** — it's a flatten of data the page already fetches.

What I invented and has no field behind it: per-connection item counts on the list (`event_count` is deliberately omitted from list responses), "62 items behind", tool usage counts, Gmail label counts at setup, and all of plates 15/16 — `InferenceProviderItem` is only `{slug, kind, displayName, capabilities, hasCustomUpstream, isDefault, status, createdAt}` and `SandboxItem` only `{name, providerKind, connected, details, config}`. No spend, no latency, no session counts.

What I under-used and is real: `AvailableOperationItem` gives real operation names, `kind: read|write`, and `requires_approval`. `FeedRunItem` gives `items_collected` per run. `FeedItem.event_count` is real (only the *connection* list omits it). `AuthProfileItem` has `expires_at` / `is_expired` / `granted_scopes`. `ChannelFeedMessage` is `{timestamp, user, text, isBot}` — exactly the transcript.

Rebuilding every plate against those fields, with a **Data source** line on each naming the hook and fields so you can check it, plus click-through navigation.

  --serif: Charter, "Bitstream Charter", "Iowan Old Style", "Palatino Linotype", Palatino, Georgia, serif;
  --sans: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "SF Pro Text", "Segoe UI", Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif;
  --mono: ui-monospace, "SF Mono", SFMono-Regular, Menlo, "JetBrains Mono", monospace;
}
@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark){
  :root{
    --ground:#101219; --ground-2:#0A0C11; --surface:#171A22; --surface-2:#1C202A;
    --line:#272B35; --line-soft:#1F232C;

    --signal:#D9A24E; --signal-soft:#33291A;
    --ok:#68A87E; --ok-soft:#1B2A21;
    --warn:#CFA04A; --warn-soft:#2C2517;
    --bad:#CC6E63; --bad-soft:#2E1D1B;
    --shadow:0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,.4), 0 12px 32px -14px rgba(0,0,0,.7);
  }
}
:root[data-theme="dark"]{
  --ground:#101219; --ground-2:#0A0C11; --surface:#171A22; --surface-2:#1C202A;
  --line:#272B35; --line-soft:#1F232C;
  --ink:#E7E8EC; --ink-2:#B6BAC4; --muted:#848896; --faint:#666B78;
  --signal:#D9A24E; --signal-soft:#33291A;
  --ok:#68A87E; --ok-soft:#1B2A21; --warn:#CFA04A; --warn-soft:#2C2517;
  --bad:#CC6E63; --bad-soft:#2E1D1B;
  --shadow:0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,.4), 0 12px 32px -14px rgba(0,0,0,.7);
}
:root[data-theme="light"]{
  --ground:#F6F5F2; --ground-2:#EDECE7; --surface:#FFFFFF; --surface-2:#FAF9F6;
  --line:#DEDCD5; --line-soft:#EBE9E3;
  --ink:#1B1D22; --ink-2:#474B55; --muted:#7C808C; --faint:#A2A5AE;
  --signal:#A2661A; --signal-soft:#F2E6D2;
  --ok:#3D7A52; --ok-soft:#E2EDE5; --warn:#9E7119; --warn-soft:#F4EAD3;
  --bad:#A54339; --bad-soft:#F5E2DF;
  --shadow:0 1px 2px rgba(27,29,34,.05), 0 8px 24px -12px rgba(27,29,34,.18);
}

*{box-sizing:border-box;}
html{scroll-behavior:smooth;}
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce){html{scroll-behavior:auto;} *{animation:none !important; transition:none !important;}}
body{margin:0; background:var(--ground); color:var(--ink); font-family:var(--sans); font-size:16px; line-height:1.6; -webkit-font-smoothing:antialiased;}
:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--signal); outline-offset:2px; border-radius:3px;}

.wrap{max-width:1180px; margin:0 auto; padding:0 28px;}

/* ---------- top bar ---------- */
.topbar{position:sticky; top:0; z-index:60; background:color-mix(in srgb, var(--ground) 90%, transparent); backdrop-filter:blur(12px); border-bottom:1px solid var(--line);}
.topbar-in{max-width:1180px; margin:0 auto; padding:9px 28px; display:flex; align-items:center; gap:18px;}
.topbar-mark{font-family:var(--mono); font-size:11px; letter-spacing:.12em; text-transform:uppercase; color:var(--muted); white-space:nowrap;}
.jump{display:flex; gap:2px; overflow-x:auto; flex:1; min-width:0; scrollbar-width:none;}
.jump::-webkit-scrollbar{display:none;}
.jump a{font-family:var(--mono); font-size:11px; text-decoration:none; color:var(--muted); padding:4px 7px; border-radius:4px; white-space:nowrap; transition:color .12s, background .12s;}
.jump a:hover{color:var(--ink); background:var(--ground-2);}
.jump a.here{color:var(--signal); background:var(--signal-soft);}

/* ---------- masthead ---------- */
.mast{padding:74px 0 20px;}
.mast .eyebrow{font-family:var(--mono); font-size:11px; letter-spacing:.16em; text-transform:uppercase; color:var(--signal); margin:0 0 18px;}
.mast h1{font-family:var(--serif); font-weight:600; font-size:clamp(36px,5.2vw,58px); line-height:1.05; letter-spacing:-.018em; margin:0 0 20px; text-wrap:balance; max-width:19ch;}
.mast .lede{font-family:var(--serif); font-size:20px; line-height:1.55; color:var(--ink-2); max-width:64ch; margin:0 0 14px;}
.mast .lede strong{color:var(--ink); font-weight:600;}
.rule{height:1px; background:var(--line); border:0; margin:0;}

/* ---------- how to use ---------- */
.howto{display:flex; gap:14px; align-items:flex-start; border:1px solid var(--line); border-radius:8px; background:var(--surface); padding:16px 20px; margin:26px 0 8px; box-shadow:var(--shadow);}
.howto .gl{font-size:15px; color:var(--signal); line-height:1.4;}
.howto p{margin:0; font-size:14.5px; color:var(--ink-2); max-width:74ch;}
.howto b{color:var(--ink);}

/* ---------- blocks ---------- */
.block{padding:52px 0;}
.block h2{font-family:var(--serif); font-weight:600; font-size:29px; letter-spacing:-.012em; margin:0 0 8px; text-wrap:balance;}
.block .sub{font-family:var(--mono); font-size:11px; letter-spacing:.14em; text-transform:uppercase; color:var(--muted); margin:0 0 22px;}
.block p{max-width:66ch; color:var(--ink-2); margin:0 0 16px;}
.block p strong{color:var(--ink); font-weight:600;}
code.k{font-family:var(--mono); font-size:.86em; background:var(--ground-2); border:1px solid var(--line-soft); border-radius:4px; padding:1px 5px; color:var(--ink);}

.maptbl{width:100%; border-collapse:collapse; margin:8px 0 26px; font-size:14px;}
.maptbl th{text-align:left; font-family:var(--mono); font-size:10px; letter-spacing:.13em; text-transform:uppercase; color:var(--muted); font-weight:500; padding:0 14px 8px 0; border-bottom:1px solid var(--line);}
.maptbl td{padding:9px 14px 9px 0; border-bottom:1px solid var(--line-soft); vertical-align:top;}
.maptbl td:first-child{font-family:var(--mono); font-size:12.5px; color:var(--ink-2); white-space:nowrap;}
.maptbl td:nth-child(2){color:var(--muted);}
.maptbl td:last-child{color:var(--ink);}

.rulecard{border:1px solid var(--line); border-left:3px solid var(--signal); background:var(--surface); border-radius:0 8px 8px 0; padding:24px 28px; margin:26px 0 8px; box-shadow:var(--shadow);}
.rulecard .lbl{font-family:var(--mono); font-size:10px; letter-spacing:.15em; text-transform:uppercase; color:var(--signal); margin:0 0 10px;}
.rulecard .stmt{font-family:var(--serif); font-size:25px; line-height:1.32; letter-spacing:-.01em; margin:0 0 14px; text-wrap:balance;}
.rulecard p{font-size:15px; margin:0; max-width:70ch;}

.twocol{display:grid; grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr; gap:32px; margin-top:24px;}
@media (max-width:820px){.twocol{grid-template-columns:1fr; gap:22px;}}
.twocol h3{font-family:var(--mono); font-size:10px; letter-spacing:.15em; text-transform:uppercase; color:var(--muted); margin:0 0 12px; padding-bottom:8px; border-bottom:1px solid var(--line);}
.tlist{list-style:none; margin:0; padding:0;}
.tlist li{font-size:14.5px; color:var(--ink-2); padding:7px 0 7px 20px; position:relative; line-height:1.5;}
.tlist li::before{content:""; position:absolute; left:0; top:14px; width:9px; height:1px; background:var(--signal);}
.tlist.cut li::before{background:var(--faint);}
.tlist.cut li{color:var(--muted);}
.tlist code{font-family:var(--mono); font-size:.87em; color:var(--ink);}

/* ---------- plates ---------- */
.plate{padding:50px 0; border-top:1px solid var(--line); scroll-margin-top:60px;}
.plate.flash > .scr{animation:pulse 1.5s ease-out;}
@keyframes pulse{0%{box-shadow:0 0 0 0 color-mix(in srgb,var(--signal) 55%,transparent), var(--shadow);} 100%{box-shadow:0 0 0 14px transparent, var(--shadow);}}
.plate-head{display:flex; align-items:baseline; gap:16px; flex-wrap:wrap; margin-bottom:4px;}
.plate-no{font-family:var(--mono); font-size:11px; letter-spacing:.13em; color:var(--signal); font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums; white-space:nowrap;}
.plate-tag{font-family:var(--mono); font-size:11px; letter-spacing:.13em; text-transform:uppercase; color:var(--muted); white-space:nowrap;}
.plate h2{font-family:var(--serif); font-weight:600; font-size:26px; letter-spacing:-.012em; margin:6px 0 8px; width:100%; text-wrap:balance;}
.plate .thesis{font-size:15.5px; color:var(--ink-2); max-width:70ch; margin:0 0 14px;}
.plate .thesis strong{color:var(--ink); font-weight:600;}

.src{font-family:var(--mono); font-size:11px; color:var(--muted); background:var(--ground-2); border:1px solid var(--line-soft); border-radius:6px; padding:8px 11px; margin:0 0 22px; line-height:1.7; overflow-x:auto;}
.src b{color:var(--signal); font-weight:500;}
.src em{color:var(--ink-2); font-style:normal;}

.notes{display:grid; grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr; gap:30px; margin-top:24px;}
@media (max-width:820px){.notes{grid-template-columns:1fr; gap:20px;}}
.notes h3{font-family:var(--mono); font-size:10px; letter-spacing:.15em; text-transform:uppercase; color:var(--muted); margin:0 0 11px; padding-bottom:7px; border-bottom:1px solid var(--line);}

/* ---------- mock screen ---------- */
.scr{border:1px solid var(--line); border-radius:10px; overflow:hidden; background:var(--surface); box-shadow:var(--shadow); font-size:13px; line-height:1.45;}
.s-bar{display:flex; align-items:center; gap:10px; padding:8px 12px; background:var(--surface-2); border-bottom:1px solid var(--line);}
.s-dots{display:flex; gap:5px;}
.s-dots i{width:9px; height:9px; border-radius:50%; background:var(--line); display:block;}
.s-url{font-family:var(--mono); font-size:10.5px; color:var(--muted); background:var(--ground-2); border:1px solid var(--line-soft); border-radius:5px; padding:2px 9px; overflow:hidden; text-overflow:ellipsis; white-space:nowrap;}
.s-body{display:flex; min-height:0;}
.s-side{width:186px; flex:none; border-right:1px solid var(--line); padding:12px 10px; background:var(--surface-2); display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:2px;}
@media (max-width:700px){.s-side{display:none;}}
.s-org{display:flex; align-items:center; gap:8px; padding:5px 6px 12px; margin-bottom:4px; border-bottom:1px solid var(--line-soft);}
.s-org b{font-size:12.5px; font-weight:600; letter-spacing:-.01em;}
.s-navitem{display:flex; align-items:center; gap:9px; padding:6px 8px; border-radius:6px; color:var(--muted); font-size:12.5px;}
.s-navitem.on{background:var(--ground-2); color:var(--ink); font-weight:500;}
.s-navitem .gl{width:14px; text-align:center; opacity:.75; font-size:12px;}
.s-navsec{font-family:var(--mono); font-size:9.5px; letter-spacing:.14em; text-transform:uppercase; color:var(--faint); padding:14px 8px 5px;}
.s-main{flex:1; min-width:0; padding:22px 26px 28px;}

.s-crumb{font-size:12px; color:var(--muted); margin-bottom:9px; display:flex; align-items:center; gap:6px; flex-wrap:wrap;}
.s-crumb .sep{color:var(--faint);}
.s-h{display:flex; align-items:flex-start; gap:12px; margin-bottom:4px;}
.s-h h1{font-size:21px; font-weight:600; letter-spacing:-.017em; margin:0; line-height:1.2;}
.s-h .grow{flex:1; min-width:0;}
.s-sub{font-size:12.5px; color:var(--muted); margin:5px 0 0;}
.s-sub .dotsep{color:var(--faint); padding:0 5px;}

.mg{width:34px; height:34px; border-radius:8px; flex:none; display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; font-weight:700; font-size:14px; color:#fff; letter-spacing:-.02em;}
.mg.sm{width:24px; height:24px; border-radius:6px; font-size:10.5px;}
.mg.xs{width:19px; height:19px; border-radius:5px; font-size:9px;}
.mg-slack{background:#4A154B;} .mg-discord{background:#5865F2;} .mg-gmail{background:#C5221F;}
.mg-github{background:#24292F;} .mg-rss{background:#E36B1E;} .mg-linear{background:#5E6AD2;}
.mg-pg{background:#31648C;} .mg-hook{background:#4C5563;} .mg-dir{background:#7A6046;}
.mg-anth{background:#B4552D;} .mg-e2b{background:#2B2F3A;} .mg-tg{background:#2AABEE;}

.st{display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:5px; font-size:11.5px; font-weight:500; padding:2px 8px 2px 6px; border-radius:20px; white-space:nowrap; border:1px solid transparent;}
.st i{width:6px; height:6px; border-radius:50%; display:block; flex:none;}
.st-ok{background:var(--ok-soft); color:var(--ok); border-color:color-mix(in srgb,var(--ok) 22%, transparent);} .st-ok i{background:var(--ok);}
.st-warn{background:var(--warn-soft); color:var(--warn); border-color:color-mix(in srgb,var(--warn) 24%, transparent);} .st-warn i{background:var(--warn);}
.st-bad{background:var(--bad-soft); color:var(--bad); border-color:color-mix(in srgb,var(--bad) 24%, transparent);} .st-bad i{background:var(--bad);}
.st-idle{background:var(--ground-2); color:var(--muted); border-color:var(--line);} .st-idle i{background:var(--faint);}

.b{display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:6px; font-size:12.5px; font-weight:500; padding:5px 12px; border-radius:6px; border:1px solid var(--line); background:var(--surface); color:var(--ink); white-space:nowrap;}
.b-pri{background:var(--ink); color:var(--ground); border-color:var(--ink);}
.b-fix{background:var(--bad); color:#fff; border-color:var(--bad);}
.b-sm{font-size:11.5px; padding:3px 9px;}
.b-ghost{border-color:transparent; background:transparent; color:var(--muted);}

.s-sect{display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:space-between; gap:12px; margin:24px 0 10px; padding-bottom:8px; border-bottom:1px solid var(--line);}
.s-sect h2{font-size:13px; font-weight:600; margin:0; letter-spacing:-.005em;}
.s-sect .cnt{font-size:11.5px; color:var(--muted); font-weight:400; margin-left:7px;}

.s-rows{display:flex; flex-direction:column;}
.s-row{display:flex; align-items:center; gap:11px; padding:10px 8px; border-bottom:1px solid var(--line-soft); margin:0 -8px;}
.s-row:last-child{border-bottom:0;}
.s-row .nm{font-size:13px; font-weight:500; letter-spacing:-.005em;}
.s-row .mt{font-size:11.5px; color:var(--muted); margin-top:1px;}
.s-row .grow{flex:1; min-width:0;}
.s-row .rt{font-size:11.5px; color:var(--muted); font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums; text-align:right; white-space:nowrap;}
.s-row.hl{background:var(--ground-2); border-radius:6px;}
.s-group{font-family:var(--mono); font-size:9.5px; letter-spacing:.13em; text-transform:uppercase; color:var(--faint); padding:16px 0 6px;}

.s-strip{display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; border:1px solid var(--line); border-radius:8px; background:var(--surface-2); overflow:hidden; margin-top:16px;}
.s-strip > div{flex:1; min-width:118px; padding:11px 14px; border-right:1px solid var(--line);}
.s-strip > div:last-child{border-right:0;}
.s-strip dt{font-family:var(--mono); font-size:9.5px; letter-spacing:.12em; text-transform:uppercase; color:var(--muted); margin:0 0 4px;}
.s-strip dd{margin:0; font-size:13px; font-weight:500; font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums;}

.s-ban{display:flex; align-items:flex-start; gap:11px; padding:12px 14px; border-radius:8px; border:1px solid; margin-top:16px; font-size:12.5px; line-height:1.5;}
.s-ban.bad{background:var(--bad-soft); border-color:color-mix(in srgb,var(--bad) 30%,transparent); color:var(--ink);}
.s-ban.warn{background:var(--warn-soft); border-color:color-mix(in srgb,var(--warn) 30%,transparent); color:var(--ink);}
.s-ban.info{background:var(--ground-2); border-color:var(--line); color:var(--ink-2);}
.s-ban b{display:block; font-weight:600; margin-bottom:2px; color:var(--ink);}
.s-ban .grow{flex:1; min-width:0;}
.s-ban .gl{font-size:14px; line-height:1.2;}

.s-disc{margin-top:22px; border-top:1px solid var(--line); padding-top:12px; display:flex; align-items:center; gap:8px; color:var(--muted); font-size:12.5px;}
.s-disc .car{font-size:10px; color:var(--faint);}

.s-chips{display:flex; gap:6px; flex-wrap:wrap; margin:14px 0 4px;}
.s-chip{font-size:11.5px; padding:3px 10px; border-radius:20px; border:1px solid var(--line); color:var(--muted); background:var(--surface);}
.s-chip.on{background:var(--ink); color:var(--ground); border-color:var(--ink); font-weight:500;}

.s-ops{display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:6px; margin-top:4px;}
.s-op{font-family:var(--mono); font-size:11px; padding:3px 8px; border-radius:5px; background:var(--ground-2); border:1px solid var(--line-soft); color:var(--ink-2);}
.s-op.w{border-color:color-mix(in srgb,var(--warn) 34%,transparent); color:var(--warn);}

.s-cat{display:grid; grid-template-columns:repeat(3,1fr); gap:8px; margin-top:12px;}
@media (max-width:700px){.s-cat{grid-template-columns:repeat(2,1fr);}}
.s-card{border:1px solid var(--line); border-radius:8px; padding:11px 12px; background:var(--surface); display:flex; gap:9px; align-items:flex-start;}
.s-card .nm{font-size:12.5px; font-weight:500; letter-spacing:-.005em;}
.s-card .ds{font-size:11px; color:var(--muted); margin-top:2px; line-height:1.4;}

.s-field{margin-top:14px;}
.s-field label{display:block; font-size:12px; font-weight:500; margin-bottom:5px; color:var(--ink);}
.s-field .hint{font-size:11.5px; color:var(--muted); margin-top:5px; line-height:1.45;}
.s-input{border:1px solid var(--line); border-radius:6px; background:var(--surface-2); padding:7px 11px; font-size:12.5px; color:var(--muted);}
.s-input.mono{font-family:var(--mono); font-size:11.5px;}
.s-input.blk{display:block; width:100%;}

.s-msg{display:flex; gap:9px; padding:9px 0; border-bottom:1px solid var(--line-soft);}
.s-msg:last-child{border-bottom:0;}
.s-msg .who{font-size:12.5px; font-weight:600; letter-spacing:-.005em;}
.s-msg .tm{font-size:10.5px; color:var(--faint); margin-left:7px; font-weight:400;}
.s-msg .tx{font-size:12.5px; color:var(--ink-2); margin-top:2px; line-height:1.5;}
.av{width:24px; height:24px; border-radius:50%; flex:none; background:var(--ground-2); border:1px solid var(--line); display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; font-size:10px; font-weight:600; color:var(--muted);}

.s-code{font-family:var(--mono); font-size:11px; background:var(--ground-2); border:1px solid var(--line-soft); border-radius:6px; padding:9px 11px; color:var(--ink-2); overflow-x:auto; white-space:pre; margin-top:8px; line-height:1.6;}

/* ---------- clickable affordance inside mocks ---------- */
.scr a{color:inherit; text-decoration:none;}
a.go{cursor:pointer; transition:background .12s, border-color .12s, color .12s;}
a.go.s-row:hover{background:var(--ground-2); border-radius:6px;}
a.go.s-card:hover{border-color:var(--ink);}
a.go.b:hover{border-color:var(--ink); }
a.go.b-pri:hover{opacity:.85;}
a.go.b-fix:hover{opacity:.85;}
a.go.s-crumb-l:hover{color:var(--ink); text-decoration:underline;}
a.go.s-disc:hover{color:var(--ink);}
a.go.s-ban:hover{border-color:var(--ink);}
.scr a.go[data-hint]{position:relative;}

/* ---------- follow-me pill ---------- */
.pill{
  position:fixed; right:20px; bottom:20px; z-index:80;
  display:none; align-items:center; gap:10px;
  background:var(--surface); border:1px solid var(--line); border-radius:999px;
  padding:7px 8px 7px 14px; box-shadow:var(--shadow);
  font-family:var(--mono); font-size:11px; letter-spacing:.06em; color:var(--muted);
  max-width:min(90vw, 420px);
}
.pill.on{display:flex;}
.pill .where{white-space:nowrap; overflow:hidden; text-overflow:ellipsis; color:var(--ink);}
.pill button{
  font-family:var(--mono); font-size:11px; letter-spacing:.06em;
  border:1px solid var(--line); background:var(--ground-2); color:var(--ink);
  border-radius:999px; padding:4px 11px; cursor:pointer; white-space:nowrap;
}
.pill button:hover{border-color:var(--ink);}
.pill button[disabled]{opacity:.4; cursor:default;}

/* ---------- ledger ---------- */
.ledger{width:100%; border-collapse:collapse; font-size:14px; margin-top:10px;}
.ledger th{text-align:left; font-family:var(--mono); font-size:10px; letter-spacing:.13em; text-transform:uppercase; color:var(--muted); font-weight:500; padding:0 16px 8px 0; border-bottom:1px solid var(--line);}
.ledger td{padding:10px 16px 10px 0; border-bottom:1px solid var(--line-soft); vertical-align:top;}
.ledger td:first-child{font-family:var(--mono); font-size:12px; color:var(--ink); white-space:nowrap;}
.ledger td:nth-child(2){color:var(--muted);}
.ledger td:last-child{color:var(--ink-2);}
.tblscroll{overflow-x:auto;}

.q{border:1px solid var(--line); border-radius:8px; background:var(--surface); padding:20px 24px; margin-top:14px; box-shadow:var(--shadow);}
.q .qn{font-family:var(--mono); font-size:10px; letter-spacing:.14em; color:var(--signal); text-transform:uppercase; margin:0 0 8px;}

<div class="wrap">

  <header class="mast">
    <p class="eyebrow">Proposal · unbuilt · no API changes</p>
    <h1>One screen per decision, not one tab per table.</h1>
    <p class="lede">The connector pages today are a projection of the schema. Six tables became six tabs, and for a chat connector four of the eight resulting cells render an empty state.</p>
    <p class="lede">Seventeen plates covering every page, connector type, and subpage. <strong>Every value shown comes from a field the API already returns</strong> — each plate lists its hook and fields so you can check it. Where a number would need new backend work, the plate does without it.</p>

    <div class="howto">
      <span class="gl">▶</span>
      <p><b>This is clickable.</b> Buttons, rows, and breadcrumbs inside the mock screens navigate to the plate they would lead to in the real product. Follow a path from the index through setup into a connection; the pill at bottom-right tracks where you are and takes you back.</p>
    </div>
  </header>

  <hr class="rule">

  <section class="block">
    <h2>What the pages do today</h2>
    <p class="sub">Diagnosis</p>
    <p>Tabs are named after storage, so the same four words mean different things at each depth, and the middle slot swaps <code class="k">Connections</code>↔<code class="k">Feeds</code> so the bar does not resize. A layout constraint became the information architecture.</p>
    <div class="tblscroll">
      <table class="maptbl">
        <thead><tr><th>Table</th><th>Became</th><th>Becomes</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>connector_definition</td><td>Connector page + 4 tabs</td><td>A catalog entry, and an admin panel</td></tr>
          <tr><td>connection</td><td>Connections tab → page + 4 tabs</td><td>The page. The only page.</td></tr>
          <tr><td>feed</td><td>Feeds tab → its own route depth</td><td>A section, opening in place</td></tr>
          <tr><td>operation</td><td>Actions tab, empty for chat</td><td>A section, absent at zero</td></tr>
          <tr><td>run</td><td>Overview tab with kind filters</td><td>Sync history inside its source</td></tr>
          <tr><td>auth_profile</td><td>Settings, and a 2,777-line form</td><td>Setup, then quiet until it breaks</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </div>

    <div class="rulecard">
      <p class="lbl">The premise</p>
      <p class="stmt">A screen per user decision, not a tab per table.</p>
      <p>Four decisions: connect something, choose what it can see, fix it when it breaks, disconnect. Two things people read: is it healthy, and what does it give my agents. Everything else is evidence, and evidence earns space only when it explains a state someone has to act on.</p>
    </div>

    <div class="twocol">
      <div>
        <h3>Structural moves</h3>
        <ul class="tlist">
          <li>Connection is the noun. The list is accounts, not connector types.</li>
          <li>No tab bar. Sections render only when non-empty.</li>
          <li>Feeds stop being a route depth and open in place.</li>
          <li><code>/connectors/github</code> with one connection redirects to it.</li>
          <li>The connector level survives as <strong>Manage app</strong>, for admins.</li>
          <li>Eleven filter chips collapse to three, on one axis.</li>
        </ul>
      </div>
      <div>
        <h3>Why no API change is needed</h3>
        <ul class="tlist">
          <li><code>useConnections(orgId)</code> already returns every connection with <code>status</code>, <code>error_message</code>, <code>feed_count</code>, <code>operations_summary</code>, and the device fields.</li>
          <li>The index already fetches connections — <code>useConnectionConnectorGroups</code> nests them inside groups. Plate 01 is a flatten.</li>
          <li><code>FeedItem</code> carries <code>event_count</code>, <code>last_sync_at</code>, <code>next_run_at</code>, <code>kind</code>, <code>target_agent_id</code>.</li>
          <li><code>AvailableOperationItem</code> carries real names, <code>kind: read|write</code>, and <code>requires_approval</code>.</li>
        </ul>
      </div>
    </div>
  </section>

<!-- ============ PLATE 03 ============ -->
<section class="plate" id="p03">
  <div class="plate-head"><span class="plate-no">03/17</span><span class="plate-tag">Setup · managed install</span></div>
  <h2>When Lobu owns the OAuth app, setup is one button</h2>
  <p class="thesis">Slack's definition declares three auth methods: <code class="k">app_installation</code>, <code class="k">oauth</code>, and <code class="k">none</code>. Most people want the first. The screen leads with it and files the rest under a disclosure, instead of opening with a method picker.</p>
  <p class="src"><b>connector def .authSchema.methods</b> → <em>type, label, description</em> · <b>AuthProfileItem.requested_scopes</b> → <em>the scope list, rewritten as consequences</em></p>

  <div class="scr">
    <div class="s-bar"><div class="s-dots"><i></i><i></i><i></i></div><div class="s-url">lobu.ai/acme/connectors/add/slack</div></div>
    <div class="s-body">
      <main class="s-main">

        <div class="s-h">
          <span class="mg mg-slack">S</span>

        <li><code>display_name</code> asked up front. It defaults to the workspace name and is editable later.</li>
        <li>App-profile and account-profile selects with inline create-profile forms.</li>

<!-- ============ PLATE 05 ============ -->
<section class="plate" id="p05">

  <h2>When there is no OAuth, the screen is a recipe</h2>
  <p class="thesis">Discord declares <code class="k">auth: none</code> and takes three values from its options schema. That is genuinely three fields of typing, so the job is to make them findable rather than to hide them. Each hint gives the exact path inside Discord's portal.</p>
  <p class="src"><b>connector def .options_schema.properties</b> → <em>botToken (format:password), applicationId, publicKey</em> · <b>x-lobu-chat-platform: "discord"</b> → <em>the inbound endpoint</em></p>

  <div class="scr">
    <div class="s-bar"><div class="s-dots"><i></i><i></i><i></i></div><div class="s-url">lobu.ai/acme/connectors/add/discord</div></div>
    <div class="s-body">
      <main class="s-main">
        <div class="s-crumb"><a class="go s-crumb-l" href="#p01">Connectors</a><span class="sep">›</span><a class="go s-crumb-l" href="#p02">Add</a><span class="sep">›</span><span>Discord</span></div>
        <div class="s-h">
          <span class="mg mg-discord">D</span>
          <div class="grow"><h1>Connect Discord</h1><p class="s-sub">Discord has no sign-in flow for bots. You create the bot, then paste its credentials here.</p></div>
        </div>

        <div class="s-ban info">
          <span class="gl">①</span>
          <div class="grow"><b>Create a Discord application first</b>Open the developer portal, create an application, add a bot, and keep the tab open. All three values below are on that page.</div>
          <span class="b b-sm">Open portal ↗</span>
        </div>

        <div class="s-field"><label>Bot token</label><span class="s-input blk mono">••••••••••••••••••••••••••••••</span>
          <p class="hint">Bot → Token → Reset Token. Discord shows it once.</p></div>
        <div class="s-field"><label>Application ID</label><span class="s-input blk mono">1284…</span>
          <p class="hint">General Information → Application ID.</p></div>
        <div class="s-field"><label>Public key</label><span class="s-input blk mono">a3f9…</span>

        <div class="s-ban warn" style="margin-top:16px">
          <span class="gl">②</span>
          <div class="grow"><b>Then point Discord at Lobu</b>Set the Interactions Endpoint URL to <code style="font-family:var(--mono); font-size:11.5px">https://lobu.ai/hooks/discord/acme</code></div>

        </div>

        <div style="margin-top:20px"><a class="b b-pri go" href="#p06">Connect</a></div>
      </main>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="notes">
    <div>
      <h3>Decisions this screen serves</h3>
      <ul class="tlist">

        <li>The hints name the portal navigation path, which is where this setup actually fails.</li>
        <li>The callback URL sits beside the fields it pairs with, not discovered later in Settings.</li>
      </ul>
    </div>
    <div>
      <h3>Gone from this screen</h3>
      <ul class="tlist cut">
        <li>A generic JSON-schema renderer emitting three unlabelled password inputs.</li>
        <li>Auth-profile creation UI, <code>name</code> plus <code>profile-slug</code>, beside the credentials.</li>
        <li>Device select and CDP URL fields, which have nothing to do with Discord.</li>

    </div>

</section>

<script>
(function () {
  var stack = [];
  var pill = document.getElementById('pill');
  var pillWhere = document.getElementById('pill-where');
  var pillBack = document.getElementById('pill-back');
  var pillTop = document.getElementById('pill-top');
  var suppress = false;

  function labelFor(id) {
    var el = document.getElementById(id);
    if (!el) return id;
    var no = el.querySelector('.plate-no');
    var tag = el.querySelector('.plate-tag');
    if (no && tag) return no.textContent.trim() + '  ' + tag.textContent.trim();
    var h = el.querySelector('h2');
    return h ? h.textContent.trim() : id;
  }

  function flash(id) {
    var el = document.getElementById(id);
    if (!el || !el.classList.contains('plate')) return;
    el.classList.remove('flash');
    void el.offsetWidth;
    el.classList.add('flash');
  }

  function markJump(id) {
    var links = document.querySelectorAll('.jump a');
    for (var i = 0; i < links.length; i++) {
      links[i].classList.toggle('here', links[i].getAttribute('href') === '#' + id);
    }
  }

  function showPill(id) {
    pillWhere.textContent = labelFor(id);
    pill.classList.add('on');
    pillBack.disabled = stack.length === 0;
    markJump(id);
  }

  function currentPlate() {
    var plates = document.querySelectorAll('.plate, .block[id]');
    var best = null;
    for (var i = 0; i < plates.length; i++) {
      var r = plates[i].getBoundingClientRect();
      if (r.top <= 140) best = plates[i];
    }
    return best ? best.id : null;
  }

  document.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
    var a = e.target.closest ? e.target.closest('a[href^="#"]') : null;
    if (!a) return;
    var id = a.getAttribute('href').slice(1);
    if (!id || !document.getElementById(id)) return;
    // Only mock-internal links push onto the trail; the top nav is a jump, not a step.
    if (a.classList.contains('go')) {
      var from = currentPlate();
      if (from && from !== id) stack.push(from);
    }
    e.preventDefault();
    suppress = true;
    document.getElementById(id).scrollIntoView({ block: 'start' });
    history.replaceState(null, '', '#' + id);
    flash(id);
    showPill(id);
    setTimeout(function () { suppress = false; }, 600);
  });

  pillBack.addEventListener('click', function () {
    var id = stack.pop();
    if (!id) return;
    suppress = true;
    document.getElementById(id).scrollIntoView({ block: 'start' });
    history.replaceState(null, '', '#' + id);
    flash(id);
    showPill(id);
    setTimeout(function () { suppress = false; }, 600);
  });

  pillTop.addEventListener('click', function () {
    stack.length = 0;
    window.scrollTo({ top: 0 });
    pill.classList.remove('on');
  });

  var ticking = false;
  window.addEventListener('scroll', function () {
    if (suppress || ticking) return;
    ticking = true;
    requestAnimationFrame(function () {
      ticking = false;
      var id = currentPlate();
      if (!id) { pill.classList.remove('on'); return; }
      pillWhere.textContent = labelFor(id);
      pill.classList.add('on');
      pillBack.disabled = stack.length === 0;
      markJump(id);
    });
  }, { passive: true });

  if (location.hash && document.getElementById(location.hash.slice(1))) {
    showPill(location.hash.slice(1));
  }
})();
</script>

Same URL, rebuilt: **https://claude.ai/code/artifact/503f8363-d9ca-458c-9126-21169b8e656b**

**On your question** — yes, and it makes the case easier. `useConnectionConnectorGroups` already returns connections, just nested one level down inside groups. And `useConnections(orgId)` with no filter returns the flat list with `status`, `error_message`, `feed_count`, `operations_summary`, and the device fields. Plate 01 is a flatten of data the page already fetches, not a new endpoint.

**On the API constraint** — every plate now carries a **Data source** line naming the hook and the exact fields it reads, so you can check each screen against the type. Three plates changed materially:

Plate 01 lost its item counts. `event_count` is deliberately omitted from list responses (the per-row anti-join was 1303ms vs 2.3ms), so rows now read "2 sources · 9 tools" from `feed_count` and `operations_summary.total`. Plate 04 lost the Gmail label counts — Lobu doesn't call Gmail at setup time, so the labels are offered as choices from the schema's own description with free text kept as a fourth option. Plates 15 and 16 were mostly invented and are rewritten from the real payloads: `InferenceProviderItem` gives `capabilities`, `isDefault`, `hasCustomUpstream` and nothing else, so the provider page leads with the default flag and modality support; `SandboxItem` gives `connected` and `details`, so the sandbox page is a credential and a boundary. No spend, no latency, no denied-tool telemetry — where I'd invented a number, the plate now says so in its source line.

Going the other way, four real fields the current UI ignores now earn their place: `requires_approval` and `operations_summary.reads/writes` drive the read/write split on plate 08, `repair_attempt_count` becomes "Lobu has retried 6 times" on the broken plate, and `FeedRunItem.items_collected` becomes the sync history on plate 13.

**On interactivity** — the mock screens are click-through. "Add connector" goes to the catalog, a catalog card goes to that connector's setup, "Add to Slack" lands on the connected chat page, a connection row opens its plate, breadcrumbs walk back up. The pill bottom-right tracks where you are and keeps a trail, so `01 → 02 → 03 → 06 → 14` and back works as a path. The top nav is a jump rather than a step, so it doesn't pollute the trail.

I also cut the copy back — the self-congratulatory framing ("proves the model holds", "the pattern worth stealing", "the state that matters most and gets the least design") is gone, theses are shorter, and em-dashes are mostly out.

**Confidence: high on API accuracy, medium-high on the design.** I read the actual type definitions for `ConnectionItem`, `FeedItem`, `FeedRunItem`, `OperationSummary`, `AvailableOperationItem`, `AuthProfileItem`, `ChannelFeedMessage`, `InferenceProviderItem`, and `SandboxItem`, plus the real connector definitions in `packages/connectors/src` — every field named is one I read. content.text:
Read it. Clear verdict: **its top level is better than mine, its detail level is worse.**

**Take the resource split.** Connectors / Devices / Models / Runtimes as peers is right, and it kills the weakest thing in my version — I stapled "Runtime & models" to the bottom of the connectors list, which is a half-measure that keeps pretending a model provider is a connection. The prototype's line, "stop treating everything as a connector," is the same argument my plates 15 and 16 make, just followed all the way through.

**It's right about Devices and I was wrong.** I made the device a property of a connection (plate 10). It's the other way round. `/api/me/devices` returns `DeviceWorkerItem` with `capabilities[]`, `connector_count`, `connector_error_count`, `last_sync_at`, and a `connectors[]` array of cross-links back into connections. One device hosts many connectors, it has its own endpoint, and its own failure mode. It's a first-class resource and the prototype models it correctly.

**Take "Needs attention."** Same instinct as my broken-first sort, but it works better at hub level because it spans four resource types — offline device, connection needing repair, unavailable browser session. My version can only surface the connector-shaped problems.

**Leave the detail tabs.** This is where the complexity you felt comes from. Gmail gets `Overview | Data | Actions | Activity | Advanced`, Telegram gets `Overview | Routing | Access | Activity | Advanced`, Device gets `Overview | Capabilities | Connectors | Activity | Advanced`, Model gets `Overview | Models | Routing | Agents | Advanced`. Five types, five tabs each, and the middle three change every time. You learn a new bar on every page. That's the current app's problem re-lettered, not solved — tabs still named after subsystems rather than decisions.

Two specific smells in there. **"Advanced"** on every type means "the fields we couldn't place" — it's the drawer the 2,777-line form gets swept into. And **"Activity"** as a per-object tab recreates the runs table I removed; Activity is already a top-level section, so this is the second place the same data lives.

And structurally: at a connection detail you're reading *two* stacked tab bars — resource tabs across the top, detail tabs below — before any content. That's the complexity, and it's not buying anything.

So the synthesis is clean: **its top level, my detail level.** Four resources as peers, each a list, "needs attention" spanning them; every detail page a single scrolling column whose sections appear only when non-empty.

One fork I'd want your call on before I rebuild, because it changes the shape:

Does **Connect** get a hub overview page — the prototype's four summary cards plus needs-attention, sitting above the four resource lists? Or do the four resources just become four sidebar entries with no hub above them?

I lean toward **sidebar entries, no hub page**, with needs-attention folded into the top of the Connectors list. A hub is a page you pass through to get where you were going, which is the same objection that killed the connector level. But a hub earns its place if "is everything healthy?" is a question you ask often enough to deserve a destination — and with devices going offline routinely, it might be.
do you think we should have tabs or this design is better? create a html artifact that changes the page in place so i can navigate like the app

Answering the tabs question first, then building it as a real navigable app.

**No tabs on detail pages.** Tabs are the right control when three things hold: every tab has content for every instance, the set is stable across instances, and the panels are genuine peer alternatives you switch between. None of those hold here. The set changes per connector type, half the cells are empty for chat, and "what it brings in" and "what agents can do" aren't alternatives — they're a sequence you read top to bottom. Sections give you that for free, and a section can be absent, which a tab can't.

The prototype's five-tab detail bars fail the same test: `Data|Actions|Activity|Advanced` for Gmail vs `Routing|Access|Activity|Advanced` for Telegram means learning a new bar per page. Tabs survive in exactly one place — the **top-level resource split** — and even there I'd make them sidebar entries, since Connectors and Devices are separate destinations, not views of one object.

input.description: Check if the create form also creates feeds

result.output: (Bash completed with no output)

content.text:
Checked. Short answer: **the button is composed of calls that all exist, but I presented as one step something that is three today.** Here's the exact ground truth.

There is **no feed auto-provisioning** on connection create — I grepped for it. `manage_connections` action `create` makes the connection row and stops. Feeds come from a separate tool, `manage_feeds`, with `create_feed` taking `connection_id`, `feed_key`, and `config` written verbatim. And `use-connection-form.ts` never calls `manage_feeds` — so today you create the connection, land on the connection page, then separately click Add feed and fill `AddFeedForm`. Two screens, two round-trips.

So "Start syncing" is a **UX change, not an API change**. It sequences three calls the client already makes:

1. the connection already exists by then — OAuth needs a row to hang `connect_token` and the auth run off, which is why the screen can say "Signed in as burak@acme.com"
2. `create_feed` with `feed_key: "threads"`, `config: { label: "INBOX", lookback_days: 30 }` — the picker writes straight into the shape `feeds_schema["threads"].configSchema` declares, and `config` is stored verbatim
3. `trigger_feed`, which is a real action on that tool — so the label is literally true rather than aspirational

What I'd flag as the actual risk: for a connector with several declared feeds, "pick sources at setup" means N `create_feed` calls with no transaction around them. Partial failure leaves a connection with some sources and no obvious repair path. That's worth designing for before building — probably create them serially and show per-row state rather than one button that either works or doesn't.

Let me correct the screen's notes so it says this rather than implying the flow already exists.

Same URL, three things landed: **https://claude.ai/code/artifact/a7ac9efb-f7b2-4e30-abbb-9c26ec1b21aa**

## On the sidebar — you're right, I reverted it

Your reason beats my argument. A permanent nav item reads as an obligation, and if nobody needs to add a model to use Lobu, then a "Models" entry in the sidebar is actively misleading to a new user.

What I missed is that the two problems were separable all along. **Prominence** — does this look like a to-do — is solved by grouping and copy. **Shape** — a provider has no sources, channels, or tools, so it can't share the connection detail layout — is solved by giving it its own page. I conflated them, decided the shape problem required a sidebar entry, and broke your onboarding to fix a layout issue.

So they're back on the Connectors page, but as one quiet summary row per resource type under a heading doing the work:

```
Already set up for you        Nothing here needs attention to get started
  ✦ Models     Anthropic is the default, and 2 more are available    Ready
  ▣ Runtime    E2B sandbox, with the built-in runtime as fallback    Ready
  ⌘ Devices    Burak's MacBook, and 2 more                    2 of 3 online
```

Three rows instead of eight synthesized ones, and each still opens its own page shape. The subtitles reinforce it — Models says "your agents already have a working model, add a provider only if you want your own key"; Runtimes says the built-in one works out of the box. Devices only appears when you have one.

## On "Start syncing" — I overstated it

No feed auto-provisioning exists; I grepped. `manage_connections.create` makes the connection and stops, feeds come from `manage_feeds.create_feed`, and `use-connection-form.ts` never calls `manage_feeds` at all — today they're two separate screens. The button sequences calls that all exist (`create_feed`, then `trigger_feed`, which is a real action), so it's **no API change but a real flow change**. The notes panel on that screen now says so, plus the design risk: picking N sources means N `create_feed` calls with no transaction, so it should create serially with per-row state rather than being one all-or-nothing button.

## On config — that was the actual hole

You were right that I'd designed the read surfaces and hand-waved the writes. Now every type has both:

**Connection config** lives in the Settings disclosure — expand it on any connection and you get real rows, not a list of words. Gmail shows name/access/schedule/sign-in; Discord and Postgres show their secrets with Replace; the webhook shows token rotation, `titlePath`, `dedupeHeader`, and `searchable`; the device-pinned one shows which device runs it. Each row carries the field it writes.

**Source config** lives inside the expanded source row. Click Inbox on Work Gmail and you get label, window, and max-per-sync. GitHub Issues shows repository and label filter. Postgres shows the query, primary key, and cursor column. Local folders show path, file types, recursive. Virtual feeds get an explanation instead of sync history, since nothing is stored.

**Devices, models, and runtimes** each got their own Settings too.

The principle, stated in the notes on every connection page: **config lives at the level that owns it, and you edit where you read it.** Nothing navigates to a config page. That's also how the 2,777-line form distributes rather than disappears — connector picking goes to the catalog, auth methods to the per-connector setup screens, profile CRUD to Manage app, `options_schema` to connection Settings, feed config to the source row.

**Confidence: high on API grounding, medium on the code.** Every field label maps to a real column or schema path. I syntax-checked the JS but have not run it in a browser, so a click may misbehave.

Worth pushing on next: whether "Already set up for you" is the right heading, or whether that section should be collapsed by default and only expand when something in it needs attention.
isn't our chips design not ok?

Correct, they're not. Three problems, and the third is the one that makes them wrong rather than just unnecessary.

**They filter a list you can already see.** Eight connections fit on screen. A filter's job is to make an unviewable list viewable; below ~20 items it costs a click and hides things for nothing.

**I claimed a win I didn't earn.** I said I collapsed eleven chips to three "on one axis." But it's still the same `facets` object, just fewer of them — the taxonomy is still the API's, not the user's. Going from 11 API-derived chips to 3 API-derived chips is the same mistake at smaller scale.

**Data and Tools overlap, but chips say they don't.** GitHub is both. Gmail is both. Pill styling reads as a segmented control, which promises mutually exclusive sets — so clicking Data, then Tools, shows you overlapping results and no mental model forms. That's worse than no filter.

And in my own code the chips had a side effect that gives the game away: filtering hid the "Already set up for you" section entirely, because I gated it on `filter === "all"`. Filtering your connections shouldn't make your runtime disappear.

The replacement isn't a better chip set. It's: **filters are for when you can't see everything; grouping is for when you can.** The list already segments on the only axis that matters — needs you vs everything else — and that's urgency from `status`, not taxonomy from `facets`. Each row already states "2 sources · 9 tools", which answers the facet question inline without hiding anything. What's missing at scale is *lookup*, and lookup is search, not facets.

content.text:
Same URL: **https://claude.ai/code/artifact/a7ac9efb-f7b2-4e30-abbb-9c26ec1b21aa**

**Chips are now navigation.** `Connections 8 · Models 3 · Runtime 2 · Devices 2/3`, on all four list pages, with the count inline and coloured only when something needs you. "Already set up for you" is gone — the chips carry that job without a sentence explaining that a section doesn't matter. And since these are disjoint sets, the segmented styling is finally telling the truth.

**For scale, there's a "Busy workspace" toggle in the top bar.** It swaps in 34 connections — four Slack workspaces, three GitHub repos, two Gmail accounts, five webhooks — plus one Slack with 24 bound channels and one Gmail with 14 labels. Better to look at it than take my word.

Here's how it plays out, and the answer for connections is the interesting one:

**Many connections → the connector grouping comes back, but only as overflow.** When several connections share a connector, they collapse into one expandable group row (`Slack — 4 connections · 1 not active`). When a connector has one connection, it stays one row. That's `useConnectionConnectorGroups`, which the page already fetches — so the level you have today isn't wrong, it's just *mandatory* when it should be conditional. Broken items stay pinned above the grouping so they never hide inside a collapsed group, the list caps at 20 units with Show all, and search appears above 12.

**Many feeds → cap and sort by urgency.** Sources cap at 8 with a Show all, and the ones needing a person sort up — so on the 24-channel Slack, the unassigned channels are at the top, not buried at row 19. Search within appears above 12. The inline expand still works because only one is ever open.

Worth knowing the natural ceilings, because most of this rarely triggers: feeds are bounded by the connector definition for GitHub (2) and by user action for Slack (channels you bound, not all channels). RSS puts many URLs in `config.urls` on *one* feed. The genuinely unbounded cases are Gmail labels, Postgres queries, and local folders — one feed each, added deliberately.

**Confidence: high on the IA, medium on the build.** The JS syntax-checks and the grouping logic is straightforward, but I haven't run it — the busy toggle touches the most new code, so that's where a bug would be.

Two things I'd still push on: whether the group row should expand in place or navigate (in-place keeps you oriented but makes a long page longer), and whether `Runtime 2` earns a chip at all when almost nobody changes it — it may be the one that belongs in Settings rather than here.

## 5. Problem Solving

**Core diagnosis:** the connector pages are a 1:1 projection of the schema — six tables became six tabs, and for a chat connector four of eight cells render empty states. Every prior round of feedback moved margins around that structure without touching it.

**Design rule established:** *"A screen per user decision, not a tab per table."* Four decisions (connect, choose scope, fix, disconnect) and two things read (is it healthy, what does it give my agents).

**Tabs verdict:** no detail tabs — tabs require that every tab has content for every instance, the set is stable, and panels are peer alternatives. None hold. Tabs survive only at the top-level resource split, and there as chips.

* stores. We resolve it through `connections.slug` — never cast it to bigint,
 * which throws for every non-numeric (managed / slug-shaped) id.

export async function listConnectionFeeds(
	organizationId: string,
	connectionId: string,
): Promise<FeedSpec[]> {
	const sql = getDb();
	const slug = runtimeConnectionIdToSlug(connectionId);
	const rows = await sql<FeedRow>`
		SELECT
			f.id::text                            AS id,
			f.feed_key                            AS feed_key,
			f.kind                                AS kind,
			COALESCE(f.display_name, f.feed_key)  AS label,
			f.status                              AS status,
			f.virtual                             AS virtual,
			f.last_sync_at                        AS last_sync_at,
			f.items_collected                     AS items_collected,
			(
				SELECT subscription.agent_id
				FROM behavior_message_subscriptions subscription
				WHERE subscription.organization_id = f.organization_id
					AND subscription.connection_id = f.connection_id
					AND subscription.channel_id = f.feed_key
				LIMIT 1
			)                                     AS target_agent_id
		FROM feeds f
		WHERE f.organization_id = ${organizationId}
			AND f.connection_id = (
				SELECT c.id FROM connections c
				WHERE c.organization_id = ${organizationId}
					AND c.slug = ${slug}
					-- Only the LIVE row: a slug is unique per org among non-deleted
					-- connections (connections_org_slug_unique), but a soft-deleted
					-- row keeps the slug — without this the scalar subquery could
					-- match several rows and error (500).
					AND c.deleted_at IS NULL
			)
			AND f.deleted_at IS NULL
		ORDER BY COALESCE(f.last_sync_at, f.updated_at) DESC
	`;

	return rows.map((r) => ({
		id: r.id,
		feedKey: r.feed_key,
		kind: r.kind as FeedKind,
		connectionId,
		label: r.label,
		status: r.status as FeedStatus,
		virtual: r.virtual,
		lastSyncAt:
			r.last_sync_at == null ? null : new Date(r.last_sync_at).toISOString(),
		itemsCollected: Number(r.items_collected),
		targetAgentId: r.target_agent_id,
	}));
}

  created_by_user text;
  native_channel_id text;
